title: Why More Context Makes Your Agent Dumber and What to Do About It — Nupur Sharma, Qodo
summary: Give an agent your full codebase and it will attend to the start and the end, then quietly drop the middle. Nupur from Qodo calls this the U curve and builds the whole talk around it: why growing the context window did not fix the problem, and what actually does. She runs through iterative retrieval, hierarchical summarization, and self correction …
why: Direct evidence for the long-context vs retrieval debate, with concrete patterns (iterative retrieval, hierarchical summarization) you can borrow for Bloomberg search.

title: Why Eval++ Is the Next Great Compute Primitive — Sunil Pai & Matt Carrie, Cloudflare
summary: Matt Carrie and Sunil Pai from Cloudflare's agents team explain why Durable Objects turned out to be the right compute unit for AI agents: addressable, persistent, hibernating, stateful, and fast enough that 15ms London latency puts you inside a single animation frame.
why: Engineering-grade take on the runtime layer for agents — useful priors before designing multi-agent orchestration at Bloomberg, not a hype piece.

title: LLM Observability, Evaluation, Experimentation Platform — Dat Ngo, Arize
summary: Your agent called tool B before tool A, and B has a dependency on A. You did not catch it because nothing in your code audits agents. The telemetry does.
why: Agent observability is the under-discussed reliability layer — Arize's framing of non-deterministic execution paths is directly applicable to multi-agent eval.

title: LLM Research Papers: The 2026 List (January to May)
summary: A curated list of the most impactful LLM research papers from January through May 2026, organized by theme: reasoning, alignment, efficient inference, retrieval, and multi-modal.
why: Raschka filters the firehose for you — half a year of LLM research distilled to the papers worth reading, sorted by theme not date.

title: Loop Engineering
summary: Addy on the iterative pattern of building with AI: define a tight feedback loop, automate the boring parts of the loop, then increase loop frequency. Examples from his own workflow.
why: Concrete patterns for designing your own agentic dev loop — useful framing for the side project ideas you're still scoping.

title: Why Frontend Slides skill grew organically — HTML decks signal 'AI-native'
summary: Slides are inherently social — people see HTML decks and ask 'how did you make it', which makes the author look AI-native.
why: Distribution insight for your own side projects (visible artifact > silent tool) — not work-relevant but worth a 30-second read.
